applies_why: The text grades a collision in which each side presses its own multi-verse chain read together against the other's Isaiah 7:14 link (CR2 answering with 8:8 and 9:6-7, DR3 pressing the 7:16/8:3-4 bounds), which is exactly the situation K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: "never verse by verse" and "the stating-verse test DG-61 retires": reading (a) the final clause is the judge's own verdict-ground, resting UNDERDETERMINED on the single sign-verse's failure to state the mechanism in its own words, which is the retired test invoked at the judge's seat; reading (b) it merely restates DR3's pressed chain-claim, leaving the verdict wholly on the footing cross-press of the first two clauses; I weighed (a) because the clause stands after a semicolon as the judge's own unattributed assertion and supplies the reason the cross-press stays unresolved.
why: In a chain-against-chain collision the judge was required to resolve by footing alone, yet it grounded its verdict partly on the sign-verse's own silence about the mechanism, the very stating-verse test K-C retires for either side.
